scores.why: A proposes insurance-specific templates and blocks with authoring artifacts and scoped effort; B and C omit the actual page library and blur Edge Delivery development with traditional AEM components or Cloud Manager deployment.

C explicitly inventories all pages and PDFs, protects rate filings through Compliance decisions and tests old URLs; A offers a useful generic migration process while B is less accountable, and both overlook the PDF and regulatory archive requirements.

B provides WCAG 2.2 criteria, automated and manual release checks, author guidance and PDF triage, although excluding tagging and permitting noncritical defects limits completeness; A and C do not address accessibility.

B offers lean blocks, script controls, release checks and field monitoring but relies on an overly rigid Lighthouse 100 gate without explicit Core Web Vitals thresholds; C mostly repeats the score aspiration and A does not address performance.

A directly retains Akamai and specifies cache classes, purge integration, security headers and validation artifacts, while B and C leave the CDN choice open and omit the required caching, purging and header design.

C describes a relevant Compliance review process but adds separately licensed Workfront and does not demonstrate an enforceable publishing gate tied to the approved page revision; A lists loosely related review capabilities and B omits approvals entirely.

A proposes a credible sticky Akamai split, approved variants, conversion tagging and fixed statistical stopping rules with effort estimates, although assignment and consent details remain thin; B and C describe authoring setup rather than experiments.

C best addresses Drupal, Akamai, rate-filing URLs, final migration and hypercare, but leaves the actual traffic switch, rollback triggers and search directives underspecified; A and B rely on generic AEM pipeline and Dispatcher checks with weaker search protection.

B supplies a tailored prompt portfolio, competitor baseline, answer inspection, deliverables and sampling caveat; A explains relevant visibility measures with less implementation accountability, while C largely substitutes bot and referral analytics for measuring assistant descriptions.

B covers approved on-site improvements and off-site assets and outreach records, though its third-party execution method is thin; A supplies only a content production service and C mainly combines monitoring capabilities with on-site refreshes.

A directly connects approved auto, home and life comparison content to quote-start journeys with deliverables and effort; B and C offer plausible generic deployment and test processes but do not specify the requested comparison and quote behavior.

C defines source approval, removal of superseded filings, explicit rate and claim-decision refusals and secure-channel redirects; A and B discuss grounding and testing but leave the actual regulated-topic rules vague, and none fully explains enforcement beyond configuration.

A addresses Genesys routing, context mapping, testing and after-hours handling, but its separately licensed Marketo intermediary and lightly specified bridge do not establish a dependable licensed-agent integration; B and C answer an analytics question instead.

C defines question topics, drop-offs and quote starts with identity validation and delivery artifacts, although the selected event route must still be shown to expose those measures; A reports generic recommendations and purchases, while B adds intent visibility without a quote or drop-off implementation.

B maps the actual channels into schemas, connections, stitching and validated journeys with effort, but does not explain the identification events needed to stitch anonymous visitors or commit to the reporting deadline; A and C mainly describe Concierge analytics without an integrated email-and-agent design.

B gives the most tailored Snowflake CDC design with keys, versions, prerequisites and sensitive-field ownership, though refresh latency and reconciliation remain unspecified; A adds useful reconciliation and identity checks, while C offers a similar but more generic and uncosted method.

A addresses consented activity sent to Salesforce and budgets both directions but barely explains the inbound CRM implementation or Concierge-event mapping; B and C describe only CRM ingestion into CJA, with C providing clearer reconciliation and effort.

C provides the clearest Power BI dashboard specification, access design, query limits, effort and reconciliation commitment; B offers a workable but generic BI delivery process and A chiefly explains the extension and an initial numbers check.

A covers website tracking and forms plus Marketo ingestion, identity stitching, licensing and reconciliation; B largely rebuilds an existing Marketo setup without a CJA integration method, while C describes analytics ingestion but not the website connection.

C offers classification, roles and governance artifacts but storing consent and applying labels does not establish collection or activation enforcement, retention or deletion handling; A only addresses consent sign-off for audience use and B is largely unrelated analytics material.

B trains all three requested roles on their actual work, checks proficiency and leaves guides and recordings; C provides useful author training alone, and A substitutes a Coworker pilot for the required role-based enablement.
B covers permissions, tested Skills, a pilot, training for all 35 marketers and ongoing adoption with effort; A offers a useful but narrowly scoped pilot and C stops at defining workflows.

A provides relevant releases, monitoring, answer review and monthly effort but leaves the required support hours and response times as a literal placeholder; C offers only conversation review and B makes no meaningful monthly service commitment.

C specifies monthly prompt maintenance, competitive reporting, prioritized improvements, approved content volumes and effort with sampling caveats; A offers measurement concepts and experience changes without a reporting service, while B mainly provides generic content production.

notes: Repeated authoring or Concierge analytics passages sometimes replace the requested requirement entirely; those answers receive little credit regardless of their technical vocabulary.

The stronger answers connect Cedar Prairie systems and regulated content to concrete deliverables and effort, but most schedules remain build-phase labels rather than commitments to the ten- and twelve-month milestones.
Approval and human-handoff answers introduce additional Workfront or Marketo Qualifier licensing, while crucial publishing enforcement and Genesys integration details remain unproven.
Privacy responses often confuse recording consent or assigning governance labels with demonstrating collection, activation, retention and deletion controls.
All presented answers satisfy their displayed word limits under ordinary token counting, but the strongest monthly support response retains an unresolved support-hours placeholder.
